Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm 66, been farming this land for 45 years. My son works in town most of the year, sends some money back, but farming is still what feeds our family of seven. Twelve mu isn't much, so I split it — about 8 mu for wheat-maize double crop (that's our grain, can't skip it with seven mouths), and 4 mu in cotton for cash. I've done it this way for a long time.

**Wheat** (already in the ground since last October): I put down compound fertilizer before planting, maybe 40 jin per mu, then I'll topdress urea around jointing in March — another 20 jin or so. The extension technician tells us 15 kg N per mu is enough, but I usually do a bit more because I've seen wheat go yellow when you cut it too close, and that scares me more than wasting a few yuan of urea. I'll irrigate at jointing and again at grain fill, maybe one more if spring is dry. Wells are metered now, costs real money to pump, so I don't water more than I need.

**Maize** goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June — tight turnaround, sometimes only 3-4 days. No time for proper plowing, I just direct-seed into the wheat stubble with a rented planter, about 50 yuan per mu for the custom operator. One topdressing of urea at the big trumpet stage, usually one irrigation if July is dry. Maize does okay here without much fuss.

**Cotton** is more work. Planted late April. It needs careful management — bollworm, aphids, the whole thing. I'll spray maybe 4-5 times over the season. Prices have been soft the last few years, so I'm not spending big on it. Just steady management like always.
